function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **nodejs‑welcome** repo.  
It contains:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight container for the Node.js app |
| `k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/docker-image.yml` | GitHub Actions that builds & pushes the image on every push to `main` |

> **NOTE** – The repo is assumed to be a simple Express/Node.js app that listens on port **3000** (adjust if your app uses a different port).

---

## 1. Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Use the official Node.js 18 slim image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install production dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *If your entry point is different (e.g., `npm start`), change the `CMD` line accordingly.*

---

## 2. Kubernetes YAML

Create a folder `k8s/` (or any name you prefer) and add `nodejs-welcome.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # replace with your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - port: 80          # external port
    targetPort: 3000  # container port
```

> *Replace `<YOUR_REGISTRY>` with the registry you’ll push to (e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq` or `docker.io/zelarhq`).*

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add `docker-image.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **Secrets required in the repo settings**  
> * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username (or GitHub Container Registry username).  
> * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub personal access token (or GitHub PAT with `write:packages` scope).  

If you prefer GitHub Container Registry, change the `tags` line to:

```yaml
tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

and log in with:

```yaml
uses: docker/login-action@v3
with:
  registry: ghcr.io
  username: ${{ github.actor }}
  password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

---

## 4. Commit & Push

```bash
# From the root of the repo
git add Dockerfile k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml .github/workflows/docker-image.yml
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

Once pushed, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically build the image and push it to the registry you configured. The Kubernetes YAML can be applied with:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml
```

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Dockerfile |
| ✅ | Kubernetes deployment & service |
| ✅ | GitHub Actions workflow |
| ✅ | Secrets set in repo settings |
| ✅ | Files added, committed, and pushed |

That’s it! Your repo now has a fully‑functional container build pipeline and ready‑to‑deploy Kubernetes manifests. Happy coding!
